title: Per-connection rate limiting and chat spam control
description: Enforce per-connection message rate limits, chat-specific limits, and escalation (throttle → drop) so one client cannot flood the shard or the chat.
acceptanceCriteria: General message rate limit: 20 msg/s per connection (token bucket); burst allowance 40; exceeding sends {code:'rate-limited'} and drops the excess
Chat limits: 1 message per 2 s, max length 280 chars, 10 messages per 30 s sliding window
Escalation: 3 rate-limit violations in 10 s → connection dropped with code 4009 'flooded'
Flood test: a scripted client sending 100 msg/s for 10 s is throttled (server tick time unaffected: p95 tick stays < 30 ms during flood in a unit benchmark) and is dropped after escalation
Unit tests: token bucket math (accept/accept/reject sequence), chat window logic with fake timers, drop behavior on 3 violations

steps.details: src/server/ratelimit.ts: TokenBucket(rate, burst) with now() injected for testability. One bucket per WS connection, created on connect, freed on close.
Before validation/dispatch: bucket.take() → reject with rate-limited if false. Track violation timestamps; 3 within 10 s → ws.close(4009).
ChatLimiter per connection: lastSendAt (2 s min gap), sliding window (10/30 s). Chat handler checks before broadcast; violations count toward escalation.
Node ws client floods 100 msg/s at 16 other simulated entities ticking; assert p95 tick < 30 ms and client dropped by ~5 s. Unit tests with injected clock. Run full suite.

technicalNotes: Input messages (flight controls) legitimately run high-frequency; the 20 msg/s general bucket must be sized so normal play (10 Hz inputs) never trips it — verify in the e2e presence test later.
